Product

Product overview

docs/product/overview.md
  • Platform
  • Transactions & import
  • Budgets

  • CPF
  • Insurance
  • AI (ADR 0004)
  • Notifications (extensible)

  • Build approach

Source of truth for scope. user-stories.md = testable form. Updated 2026-11-18.

Pitch: SG personal finance — spending, budgets, goals, CPF projection, insurance in one picture. CPF is first-class: gross salary says little about spendable pay (age bracket, OW ceiling, bonus/AW interaction). Generic apps get this wrong.

Platform

iOS → web soon after → Android later (ADR 0002). Expo/RN from day one (ADR 0001).

Transactions & import

  • CSV import from SG banks (DBS, OCBC, UOB, …).
  • AI auto-categorises imported rows.
  • Preset category list; user can rename/add/delete.
  • Option: AI generates categories + sub-categories from CSV.
  • Manual entry supported.

Budgets

  • Per-category, configurable month-end behaviour:
    • Auto-rollover — unused carries forward silently.
    • Ask me — month-end prompt: roll over / move to goal / reset.
    • Reset — back to base each month.
  • Balance = base + accumulated rollover (pot grows if underspent).
  • A category can act as a sinking fund (contribute; don't spend until target).

Goals

  • Name, target, monthly contribution → progress + projected completion date.
  • Notify when reached (user then buys).
  • Top-level, separate from budgets, same "pot" mechanic.

CPF

  • Inputs: DOB + gross monthly salary.
  • Computes: employee deduction (age-based, 20% ≤55 → 5% >70), employer (17% ≤55 → 7.5% >70), split across OA/SA/MA/RA by age, take-home pay.
  • OW ceiling $8,000/mo (Jan 2026, unverified).
  • Bonus logged separately; CPF via AW ceiling (~$102k/yr − OW contributed YTD).
  • User enters OA/SA/MA balances once; app projects forward.
  • Milestones: MA → BHS $79k (overflow changes) · SA/RA → FRS $220.4k / BRS $110.2k · OA $20k investment threshold · top-up tax relief $8k/yr · extra 1% on first $60k combined.
  • All figures: see ../reference/cpf-rules.md (unverified).

Insurance

  • Free-form: name policy, upload docs (PDF/image).
  • Tracks premiums paid over time.
  • AI parses docs → coverage details + type: ISP (health) · Life (term/whole) · CI · DI · ILP · General (travel/car/home).
  • Per-type UI: what user has + financial impact.
  • Coverage gap analysis vs life goals and spending.

AI (ADR 0004)

  • Rule-based alerts always on, no key: budget thresholds, large txns, savings rate.
  • BYOK: OpenAI / Anthropic / Google.
  • Standardised system prompt + injected context (salary, goals, CPF, insurance) for consistent behaviour across models.
  • Digest on schedule: on-demand / weekly / monthly / biannual.
  • On-demand chat over own data.

Notifications (extensible)

Budget threshold (e.g. 80%) · goal reached · CPF milestone · premium due · month-end budget prompt.

Data & privacy (ADR 0003)

  • Local-first SQLite; no data leaves phone in v1 (except AI calls).
  • Repository layer so sync can be added later; future backend (self-hosted or managed) TBD.

Build approach

Design first, then Jerry builds with Claude Code.

TXN-05Grouped by day w/ running total → see rhythmChronological, date-grouped. Month selector. Smooth scroll back through months.

TXN-07Split across categories → accurate mixed purchasesLong-press/swipe → Split. Parts must sum to total.

⚠️ UNVERIFIED. Captured from conversation, not cpf.gov.sg. Ceilings change most Januaries. Verify before building the calculator; re-check every January. Wrong is worse than absent. Source: https://www.cpf.gov.sg (rates, allocation, Budget announcements).

OW ceiling$8,000/moJan 2026no

Contribution rates by age — INCOMPLETE

AgeEmployeeEmployer
≤5520%17%
55–60missingmissing
60–65missingmissing
65–70missingmissing
>705%7.5%

Account allocation — MISSING

Split across OA/SA/MA (+RA after 55) varies by age bracket. Table not captured; needed for projection.

OW vs AW (the part generic apps get wrong)

  • OW: monthly salary, capped per month at OW ceiling.
  • AW: bonus/commission, capped at annual ceiling − OW contributed YTD.
  • ⇒ a bonus's CPF depends on OW earlier that year. Huat logs bonuses as events and computes AW headroom at each.

Milestones surfaced

  • MA → BHS: overflow redirects (SA <55, RA ≥55); contribution behaviour changes.
  • SA/RA → FRS/BRS: retirement adequacy; FRS headline.
  • OA → $20k: only excess investable via CPFIS-OA.
  • Top-up headroom: unused = forgone tax relief; prompt before year end.
  • First $60k combined: +1% interest.

Derived outputs

DOB + gross monthly salary → employee deduction, employer contribution, per-account split, take-home pay (the budgeting number).

Design

Design system

docs/design/design-system.md

NOT WRITTEN. Biggest gap. Decisions live only as inline CSS in prototypes/ — unreviewable, unreusable, will be reinvented. STATUS next action #2.

Blocked on: Tokyo Riso sign-off (see prototype-notes.md).

Must contain

  • Colour tokens — semantic (surface, ink, accent, positive, negative, warning); light + dark. Gain/loss red/green must survive colour-blindness + both themes.
  • Type scale — families, weights, sizes, line heights. Tabular/lining digits for money.
  • Spacing + radius scale — discrete values only.
  • Components — transaction row, budget card w/ progress, goal progress, CPF account tile, milestone meter, stat tile, empty state, "connect a key to unlock" AI state.
  • Money formatting — SGD symbol placement, decimals, negatives (sign vs parens; never colour alone), grouping, large-number abbreviation.
  • Charts — categorical palette for spend breakdown; sequential/diverging; consistent app-wide.
  • Accessibility floor — min contrast, min touch target, no state by colour alone.

Source material

prototypes/menu-final.html (nav), prototypes/tokyo-riso.html (visual direction); cross-check screen coverage vs prototypes/index.html.

The one rule

Feature code never touches SQLite directly — only via the repository layer. Keeps "add sync later" from being a rewrite; must hold from the first screen.

PROPOSED / undecided

  • ORM/query: Drizzle vs Prisma vs raw SQL on expo-sqlite. Migrations > ergonomics — financial history can't be dropped/recreated.
  • State: React Query over repository layer — obvious, unexamined.
  • Charts: must work on RN + web; narrows options.
  • Export/import: needed early (no backup, 0003). Likely CSV + full JSON dump.
  • Auth w/o backend gives identity, not sync. Does v1 need sign-in beyond App Store expectations?

Questions to answer

  • Money: integer cents, never floats. State once, enforce everywhere.
  • Budget periods: row per month vs one row + running balance? Drives rollover + "ask me"; hardest to change later.
  • Overspend: carry negative or nothing? (only underspend specified)
  • Pots: budgets + goals one table w/ discriminator, or two? Differ on month-end.
  • CPF projection: stored rows vs derived on read? Derived more honest; stored faster and survives rate changes — history must stay accurate.
  • Rate tables as data: versioned w/ effective dates, not code constants, or history goes silently wrong (../reference/cpf-rules.md).
  • Categorisation provenance: AI vs user-set, so re-running AI doesn't clobber corrections.
  • Documents: filesystem + DB pointer vs in DB? Affects export + AI-parsing privacy question.

Decisions

0001 — Expo / React Native, cross-platform from day one

docs/decisions/0001-expo-react-native.md
  • Context
  • Decision
  • Consequences
  • Alternatives considered

Status: Accepted Date: 2026-11-18 (decided earlier; recorded on this date)

Context

Huat targets iOS first but web and Android are both planned. Jerry is building it solo with AI assistance, so maintaining separate native codebases isn't realistic.

Decision

Build on Expo / React Native from the first line of code, rather than writing a native iOS app and porting later.

Consequences

  • One codebase serves iOS, Android and web.
  • Expo handles the build and release machinery that would otherwise eat solo-dev time.
  • Accepts a performance ceiling below native. For a finance app that is mostly lists, forms and charts, this is not a real constraint.
  • Anything needing a native module may require an Expo config plugin or a dev build. Keychain/secure storage and local SQLite are all well supported.

Alternatives considered

  • Native Swift first — best iOS result, but makes web and Android a rewrite.
  • Flutter — comparable capability; React/TypeScript is the more familiar and better AI-supported ecosystem.
Decisions

0002 — iOS first, then web, Android last

docs/decisions/0002-ios-first-then-web.md
  • Context
  • Decision
  • Consequences
  • Alternatives considered

Status: Accepted Date: 2026-11-18 (decided earlier; recorded on this date)

Context

Limited solo capacity means platforms must be sequenced rather than launched together.

Decision

iOS first. Web app shortly after. Android on a longer horizon.

Consequences

  • Design and interaction decisions are made against a phone screen first; the web app will need a genuine responsive/desktop pass rather than a straight port.
  • Sign in with Apple is required from the start for App Store compliance.
  • Android-specific issues stay undiscovered for a long time. Keeping to cross-platform Expo APIs where possible limits the eventual surprise.

Alternatives considered

  • Web first — faster to ship and easier to iterate, but the product is a daily mobile habit; a web-first version would misjudge the core interactions.
Decisions

0003 — Local-first SQLite with a cloud-ready repository layer

docs/decisions/0003-local-first-sqlite.md
  • Context
  • Decision
  • Consequences
  • Alternatives considered

Status: Accepted Date: 2026-11-18 (decided earlier; recorded on this date)

Context

The app holds salary, CPF balances, full transaction history and insurance documents — about as sensitive as personal data gets. Jerry wants no server to run or secure in v1, but doesn't want to foreclose on sync across devices.

Decision

Store everything in SQLite on the device. No data leaves the phone in v1 (the one exception is AI calls, see 0004). All data access goes through a clean data/repository layer so a sync backend can be added without touching feature code.

Consequences

  • Strongest possible privacy story, and no backend cost or operational burden.
  • No cross-device sync, and no backup — losing the phone loses the data. An export/import path is needed early; this is a real v1 gap to confirm.
  • The repository layer must be respected from the start. Feature code reaching straight into SQLite is the one thing that would make later sync a rewrite.
  • Adding sync later means confronting conflict resolution, which is deferred, not solved.

Alternatives considered

  • Cloud backend from day one — gives sync and backup immediately, but means running a server holding highly sensitive financial data, for a pre-validation product.
  • Device-encrypted cloud (e.g. iCloud/CloudKit) — attractive middle ground; ties the architecture to Apple, which conflicts with 0001/0002.
Decisions

0004 — Bring-your-own-key for all AI features

docs/decisions/0004-byok-ai.md
  • Context
  • Decision
  • Consequences
  • Alternatives considered

Status: Accepted Date: 2026-11-18 (decided earlier; recorded on this date)

Context

AI categorisation, document parsing, digests and chat all need a model. Paying for inference on behalf of users means a backend, a billing relationship and per-user cost — before the product is validated.

Decision

Users connect their own OpenAI / Anthropic / Google API key. The app injects the user's financial context into a standardised system prompt so behaviour stays consistent across providers. Rule-based alerts (budget thresholds, large transactions, savings rate) are always on and need no key at all.

Consequences

  • No inference cost and no AI backend to operate.
  • Every AI feature must degrade gracefully to a "connect a key to unlock" state, and the rule-based layer has to carry real value on its own.
  • Narrows the audience: most people don't have an API key. Acceptable for v1, and a managed option can be added later without changing the architecture.
  • The key is stored on-device and must never be logged or synced.
  • A standardised system prompt across providers needs testing per provider; "works on Claude" does not mean "works on GPT".

Alternatives considered

  • App-provided inference — far better UX, but requires a backend, billing, and absorbing abuse risk pre-validation.
  • On-device models — no cost and no data leaving the phone, but quality is not yet good enough for statement categorisation or document extraction.
Decisions

0005 — Name the product "Huat"

docs/decisions/0005-name-huat.md
  • Context
  • Decision
  • Consequences
  • Alternatives considered

Status: Accepted Date: 2026-11-18

Context

The project was scaffolded as expense-tracker, which undersold a product covering CPF projection, insurance coverage, goals and AI insight. A real name was needed before design and any store listing.

Decision

Huat (發 / 发, Hokkien — "to prosper", as in huat ah). Folder, repo and all docs renamed on 2026-11-18.

Consequences

  • Warm, memorable and unmistakably Singaporean — matches an SG-only v1 audience.
  • Does not travel. The name is near-meaningless outside Singapore and the wider Hokkien-speaking diaspora. Expanding markets would mean a rename or a sub-brand; accepted knowingly.
  • Reads as playful rather than institutional. Fine for a personal-finance habit app; something to re-examine if the product ever targets institutional trust.
  • Short and clean for a bundle ID and domain.

Alternatives considered

  • nett — SG term for take-home pay, directly names the core CPF calculation. Precise but cooler in tone.
  • steady — Singlish for reliable/solid; warm, but a common word and hard to search.
  • keel — stability plus SG port heritage; too abstract without a tagline.
  • kopi, tally — both already crowded with existing apps.
Decisions

0006 — Use this repo as the cross-session second brain

docs/decisions/0006-repo-as-second-brain.md
  • Context
  • Decision
  • Consequences
  • Alternatives considered

Status: Accepted Date: 2026-11-18

Context

Design and requirements work happens across many chat sessions, with different AI assistants, on different machines, with no shared memory between them. Context was living in chat transcripts and in one assistant's local memory file — neither portable, neither durable. Work was being re-explained every session.

Decision

The Git repository is the single source of truth. A fresh session with any AI starts by reading START_HERE.md → STATUS.md, and ends by updating STATUS.md, adding a journal entry, recording ADRs, folding durable facts into the living docs, and pushing.

Structure separates three kinds of knowledge:

  • Living docs — always describe the present; edited in place.
  • Append-only history — decisions/ and journal/; never rewritten.
  • Reference data — external figures carrying as-of dates.

Consequences

  • Any AI, in any chat, can be productive within ~10 minutes of reading.
  • Decisions stop being re-litigated, which was the main tax on each new session.
  • Requires discipline: an un-pushed session is a lost session, and docs that drift out of date are worse than no docs because they are trusted.
  • Prose docs duplicate some of what code would eventually express (e.g. the data model). Accepted while there is no code; the docs must yield to code once it exists.

Alternatives considered

  • Assistant-local memory — zero effort, but locked to one tool on one machine.
  • Notion / external wiki — better editing, but splits the brain from the eventual codebase and needs an integration for each AI.
Decisions

0007 — Terse working docs + generated pretty handbook

docs/decisions/0007-terse-docs-generated-handbook.md
  • Context
  • Decision
  • Consequences
  • Alternatives

Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-18

Context

Every session re-reads the docs; prose costs context on every task. Jerry still wants complete, nicely formatted documentation for reading.

Decision

  • docs/, STATUS.md, START_HERE.md are canonical and terse (fragments, tables, all facts kept, filler dropped).
  • handbook/huat-handbook.html is generated from them by scripts/build_handbook.py (stdlib Python, no deps). Never hand-edited.
  • AI never reads/greps the handbook (or prototypes) for lookup — only when working on it. .ignore keeps both out of ripgrep.
  • Existing ADRs/journal stay as written (append-only); read order uses the decisions index instead of every ADR. New entries use terse templates.

Consequences

  • Much smaller per-session reading; one source of truth, so no drift between layers.
  • Handbook prose is as terse as its source — pretty = layout/typography, not rewritten copy.
  • Regenerating the handbook is an end-of-session step; forgetting it leaves it stale (never wrong-but-trusted for AI, since AI doesn't read it).

Alternatives

  • Hand-maintained pretty docs alongside terse ones — two sources, guaranteed drift.
  • Pretty docs only — keeps the context cost this decision removes.

Decisions made

  • 0005 — name the product Huat
  • 0006 — repo is the cross-session brain

The age-bracket rate table and the account allocation table are both incomplete — only the ≤55 and >70 endpoints are captured. This blocks the CPF calculator, which is the product's differentiator.

Process

START HERE

START_HERE.md
  • Read order
  • Two layers (ADR 0007)
  • Writing style for working docs
  • Layout
  • Rules
  • End of session (all steps)

Repo = second brain for Huat (SG personal-finance app). No app code yet. Sessions share no memory; this repo is the only continuity. Owner: Jerry.

Read order

  1. STATUS.md — phase, next actions, open questions. Always.
  2. docs/product/overview.md — scope.
  3. docs/decisions/README.md — index of settled decisions. Open an ADR only if relevant.
  4. Latest docs/journal/ entry.
  5. Whatever STATUS points to. On demand only: user-stories.md, glossary.md, reference/cpf-rules.md, architecture/, design/.

Two layers (ADR 0007)

  • docs/, STATUS.md, this file = working docs. Terse, canonical. Read/edit these.
  • handbook/huat-handbook.html = pretty docs for humans. Generated from the working docs by python3 scripts/build_handbook.py. Never read or grep it for lookup or reasoning; never hand-edit it. Touch it only when working on the handbook itself.
  • Also never read docs/design/prototypes/*.html (40–110 KB each) unless the task is the prototypes. prototype-notes.md summarises them.
  • .ignore excludes both from ripgrep/Grep.

Writing style for working docs

Fragments over sentences. Tables/bullets over prose. No preamble, no restating. Keep every fact and every "why"; drop filler. Link ADRs by number. Pretty presentation is the handbook's job, not yours.

Layout

STATUS.md  START_HERE.md  CLAUDE.md(pointer)  README.md(humans)
docs/product/      overview, user-stories, glossary
docs/reference/    external figures w/ as-of dates (cpf-rules)
docs/design/       design-system, prototype-notes, prototypes/
docs/architecture/ stack, data-model
docs/decisions/    NNNN-slug.md  append-only ADRs
docs/journal/      YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md  append-only session logs
handbook/          GENERATED pretty HTML — don't read
scripts/           build_handbook.py

Rules

  • ADRs are settled. Flag a problem once; change only via a new superseding ADR.
  • Unconfirmed ideas → mark PROPOSED. Only Jerry promotes them.
  • docs/reference/ figures carry as-of dates. Check before quoting; say if stale.
  • Living docs (STATUS, product, design, architecture, glossary) describe the present — edit in place. History (decisions, journal) — add files, never rewrite.

End of session (all steps)

  1. Update STATUS.md.
  2. Journal entry docs/journal/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md (real date; template in journal README).
  3. ADR per real decision (next number; template in decisions README).
  4. Fold durable facts into living docs (journal says that, living docs say what).
  5. python3 scripts/build_handbook.py to regenerate the handbook.
  6. Commit (descriptive message) and push. Unpushed = lost.
